champion_dev.sample_size_note: Hosmer-Lemeshow is a chi-square test whose power scales linearly with sample size N. At large retail sample sizes (N=20,952 on DEV and N=8,980 on HOLDOUT), small percentage-point deviations between coarse-binned logistic predictions and empirical decile bad rates yield statistically small p-values even when overall calibration (Brier score and portfolio mean PD) is tight.

g1_underprediction_and_g5_overprediction.g1_finding_summary: On HOLDOUT (n=8,980), Grade G1 (Score >= 565, n=1084) recorded 82 observed defaults (7.56%, 95% Jeffreys CI [6.10%, 9.25%]). Against the DEV empirical grade PD (5.67%, expected 61.42 defaults), G1 under-predicts by +189.83 bps (one-sided p = 0.0056, two-sided p = 0.0102, 99.44% confidence -> AMBER). Against the Champion continuous logistic mean PD (6.78%), G1 under-predicts by +78.41 bps (one-sided p = 0.1665, two-sided p = 0.3041 -> GREEN). Against the Platt-calibrated Challenger-Expanded mean PD (5.94%), G1 also under-predicts by +162.04 bps (one-sided p = 0.0167 -> AMBER).
g1_underprediction_and_g5_overprediction.g1_honest_root_cause_assessment: Within Grade G1, observed default rates by PAY_0 code on DEV are 3.29% (-2, n=243), 5.30% (-1, n=434), 6.06% (0, n=1,882); on HOLDOUT they are 6.25% (-2, n=96), 7.19% (-1, n=167), 7.80% (0, n=821). Code -1 is not riskier than code 0 within G1, the HOLDOUT default-rate uplift occurs across all three non-delinquent codes (-2, -1, and 0), and the Challenger (which separates -1) is also AMBER on G1. Therefore, the G1 uplift on HOLDOUT is an unexplained out-of-sample uplift, most likely sampling variation on the random 70/30 split, and is flagged for ongoing monitoring. (The merge of PAY_0 = -1 and 0 in Champion Bin 2 remains a separate portfolio-level limitation.) All figures in this sentence are generated from g1_pay0_breakdown.
g1_underprediction_and_g5_overprediction.g5_conservative_miscalibration_finding: In Grade G5 ([400, 460), n=1011 on HOLDOUT), the Champion continuous logistic mean PD is 36.01% versus an observed HOLDOUT default rate of 31.55% (-445.53 bps over-prediction; expected 364.04 vs observed 319). While G5 is GREEN on the one-sided under-prediction test (p = 0.9987) because over-prediction is capital-conservative, the two-sided binomial calibration test rejects at p = 0.003176 (and p = 0.000031 on DEV: 36.10% predicted vs 32.00% observed), identifying G5 as a conservative over-prediction miscalibration of the linear logit.
g1_underprediction_and_g5_overprediction.stated_moc_derivation_method: Under EBA/GL/2017/16 estimation-error MoC principles, each grade's Margin of Conservatism (MoC) is derived as the 95% Jeffreys credible interval upper bound on DEV minus the DEV empirical grade default rate: MoC_g = Jeffreys_95_Upper(DEV_g) - ODR_DEV_g. For G1, DEV empirical PD is 5.6663% and the DEV 95% Jeffreys upper bound is 6.6126%, yielding a derived MoC of +94.63 bps (regulatory PD = 6.6126%).

stability_psi_csi.random_split_limitation_note: DEV (n=20,952) and HOLDOUT (n=8,980) were created via a stratified random 70/30 split (random_state=42) from the same cross-sectional cohort (Taiwan, Apr-Sep 2005). Because this is a random split and NOT an out-of-time (OOT) sample, near-zero PSI and CSI values are expected by construction and only confirm proper randomisation; they are NOT evidence of portfolio or model stability over time.

approval_rule_definition.champion_rule: Approve Rating Grades G1-G4 (Champion Score >= 460, equivalent to Champion PD <= 0.268229 / 26.82%). Decline Grades G5-G6 (Score < 460).
approval_rule_definition.challenger_rule: Approve accounts with Platt-calibrated Challenger-Expanded PD <= 0.268229 (26.82%, score-equivalent >= 460).

policy_and_legal_note.legal_and_regulatory_framing: The four-fifths (80% / 0.80) disparate-impact ratio threshold is a US regulatory heuristic originating from the US EEOC Uniform Guidelines on Employee Selection Procedures (29 CFR § 1607.4D) and US ECOA fair-lending supervision. It is NOT an EU legal test. Under EU law (Charter of Fundamental Rights Art. 21, Gender Goods and Services Directive 2004/113/EC, and EBA Guidelines on Loan Origination and Monitoring EBA/GL/2020/06), direct use of protected attributes (such as SEX) is prohibited, while indirect differential impact is evaluated through objective justification, risk-based proportionality, and group calibration fairness.
